Of the unclaimed prize money on "Monopoly 200X", about three-quarters is in wins under $10,000. The game is a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

The table below shows the full count for "Monopoly 200X", with every prize level included.
696.headline: How this game pays out

762.body:
"Billion" has 1,737,770 prizes of $100 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $1 million prize, with 41 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Every line of Billion's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
762.headline: What the prize table shows

827.body:
"50th Anniversary" has one of three top prizes left and is in the last part of its run. Most of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

The most common prize left on "50th Anniversary" right now is $100.

Everything here about "50th Anniversary" comes from official Ohio lottery numbers, current through November 9.
827.headline: How far along this game is

847.body:
The $500,000 top prize on "Bingo 50X" is no longer available because all four have been claimed. The biggest prize anyone can win today is $100,000. Use that amount when you decide.

Tomorrow's count on "Bingo 50X" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
847.headline: The advertised top prize is gone

891.body:
The most common win left on "Cash Explosion 25X" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If you play "Cash Explosion 25X" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
891.headline: What's actually left to win
